title: Playground v2.5 (SDXL-arch) OpenVINO INT8 on Arc 140V — resident RAM footprint + 1024px generation speed
question: How much system RAM does Playground v2.5 (OV-INT8) occupy resident on the Arc 140V iGPU, and how fast does it generate at 1024px? Captured for UC-010's second (illustration) image model and the swap-budget math.

software.memory_sampler: psutil virtual_memory().used (system in-use), deltas vs baseline

model.name: Playground v2.5 (playgroundai/playground-v2.5-1024px-aesthetic)
model.precision: OpenVINO INT8 weight-only (optimum-cli export openvino --weight-format int8)

method: RAM: system in-use RAM sampled at baseline (with the Qwen3-Coder-30B ALSO loaded in OVMS), after Playground loads on GPU, and the peak during one 1024x1024 generation; the deltas isolate Playground (the 30B is constant in the baseline). Generation: device=GPU (Arc 140V), 1024x1024, 30 steps, guidance_scale 3.0, model-default scheduler, single image. CPU smoke (separate run): device=CPU, 512x512, 20 steps. Single run each, NOT averaged.

co_residence_finding.conclusion: Playground (~8.4 GB) co-resident with the 30B coder (~18 GB) EXCEEDS the 31.32 GB ceiling and pages ~1.2 GB to disk during generation. They cannot truly co-reside; the UC-010 design must swap one model resident per phase. Playground ALONE (~8.4 GB) fits comfortably inside 31.32 GB.

not_measured: Clean ALONE footprint (30B unloaded): the generation ran under ~1.2 GB paging pressure, so the 8.42 GB PEAK is measured under memory pressure; the 8.16 GB LOAD delta is clean (load completed before the gen paging). An alone re-measure (30B stopped) would give a publication-clean peak.
Image quality not benchmarked. Subjective: decent flat-style subjects, cluttered/painterly backgrounds; flat-vector brochure target needs background-removal or a flat-vector LoRA.
INT8 vs FP16 quality/speed not compared.
GPU power / thermal not captured this run.
